newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares ease 0.6 pct on higher inflation fears.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares ease 0.6 pct on higher inflation fears.

text.p: Istanbul shares retreated in quiet trade on Tuesday amid high overnight money and repo rates and higher inflation worries, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,940, down 12 points, or 0.61 percent from Monday. Trade volume rose up to 19.7 trillion lira ($119.5 million) from Monday's 16.8 trillion ($101.9 million).
"Lack of cash inflow is the main reason behind the fall and with the present interest rate levels, new investors are reluctant to enter the market," said Tayfun Oral from Ata Securities.
"I think the index is likely to test its support at 1,850, but investors won't be willing to sell much at that level," he addded.

Turkish Treasury met almost half of the bids in a 357-day bill auction on Tuesday by selling 257.8 trillion lira nominal valued bills at 138.38 percent yield (including witholding tax), compared to 259.9 trillion lira of 357-day bills it sold at 138.37 percent yield (including witholding tax) on August 12.
Cash shortage and central bank funding persisted in the money market while the treasury's auction caused bond yields to firm to above 120 percent level, bankers said.
Brokers said selective activity was based on mid-year financial results, most of which were released over the weekend.
